title: Performance Modeling and Comparisons of an FPGA-based Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Solver
problem: DSMC simulations encounter race conditions when parallelizing collision evaluation in conventional implementations, limiting speedup on multi-core and many-core platforms.
motivation: Microscale flow applications often require numerous repeated DSMC simulations, making acceleration critical for practical deployment.
method: The solver runs on specialized hardware (an FPGA) using a spatially-parallel collision algorithm: it divides space into regions and processes collisions region-by-region instead of letting all processors randomly evaluate collisions. This spatial organization eliminates race conditions—conflicts that occur when multiple processors simultaneously update the same data—that normally limit parallel speedup. The FPGA hardware includes custom memory layouts tailored to different particle densities, which is especially valuable for low-particle microscale simulations.
key_novelty: Organizing collision calculations spatially (dividing space into regions) prevents race conditions that normally block parallel speedup.
contributions: Novel spatially-parallel collision algorithm enabling race-condition-free DSMC execution
FPGA implementation achieving 5.5× speedup over CPU and 1.5× over GPU for low particle counts
Comprehensive performance modeling and cross-platform comparison (CPU/GPU/FPGA)
Demonstration of particular benefits for microscale flow simulations requiring repeated computations

metrics.speedup: 5.5× vs CPU, 1.5× vs GPU (low particle counts)

limitations: Evaluation focuses on low particle count microscale flows; scaling behavior and performance for larger particle systems are not discussed.
primary_theme: Parallel DSMC collision evaluation on FPGA
